summary: Formats a variable-length numeric tuple into a buffer and verifies the write. First validates via sub_565400(this, a2); on failure returns 0. Then selects a format string by which of a4/a5/a6 are non-zero: four values "(%d,%d,%d,%d)", three "(%d,%d,%d)", two "(%d,%d)", one "(%d)", and bare "%d" as a last resort when the parenthesized one-value form fails. Returns TRUE when the formatted string length equals the number of formatted arguments. Used by config, career and vehicle-file loaders as a shared tuple writer.

operations.description: Call sub_565400(this, a2) as a precondition for the whole function.
Guard on the sub_565400 result: if it returns 0, abort immediately with result 0.
Read the destination buffer pointer from this+0x180 (first argument of every format call).
When a6 is non-zero, format "(%d,%d,%d,%d)" with a3,a4,a5,a6 into the buffer via StrlenFormatCallWrapper and return (length == 4).
When a6 is zero but a5 is non-zero, format "(%d,%d,%d)" with a3,a4,a5 into the buffer and return (length == 3).
When a6 and a5 are zero but a4 is non-zero, format "(%d,%d)" with a3,a4 into the buffer and return (length == 2).
Guard on a3: if a3 is zero, return 0 (nothing to serialize).
Single value path: format "(%d)" with a3 into the buffer; return TRUE when the formatted length == 1.
Fallback single value path: when the parenthesized one-value form did not yield length 1, format "%d" with a3 and return (length == 1).
Return the result of the selected comparison (TRUE when the formatted length matches the argument count, otherwise FALSE).
